comments.text:
There two types of bread in Afghanistan that I call male bread and female bread.  Male bread is that cooked in the round pits in the ground, and tended by men in public places.  This bread is thin and quickly becomes dry.  It is very good fresh out of the oven, but after a couple of hours becomes dry and tough.  Female bread is cooked at home in a tandoori.  This is like our bread in the form of a loaf.  It is very tasty especially fresh out of the oven, and keeps moist for a day or more.  It is a real treat to get this bread.  
Yes, the pomegranates, melons, and other produce are amazingly good, apples not so much.  
Notice that the meals are mostly rice and bread.  Meat is scanty in most Afghan meals.  Most meat is chicken.   
Geography is everything in Afghanistan.  The Hindu Kush make life possible there.  Almost all Afghans live in river valleys because the land in between is desert.  Almost all the river valleys are from runoff from the Hindu Kush.  Notice the layout of a valley village.  The houses are up on the dry rocky slopes, the green fields near the river.  Flat, fertile land is precious so people live up high and walk to their fields down below.  It makes for a lot of uphill hiking so the Afghans have strong legs.  
This is a very accurate presentation, however the sorrow of the women who saw their chance of education vanish when the Taliban took over is not shown.
